title: What can you say about N-acetylcysteine (NAC) in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library gives no supported wording for N-acetylcysteine (NAC), because every claim about it is flagged for review. Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats PCOS, or restores ovulation in PCOS".

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Treats PCOS, or restores ovulation in PCOS

wordings_to_avoid.why: Promises to treat or protect an organ from damage.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Breaks up mucus, or treats bronchitis or COPD
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names diseases and describes a drug action.

evidence_gap: Every NAC claim is flagged for review because of FDA's position on NAC as a dietary ingredient (library decision of 2026-10-15; see review_flag), so the library gives no supported wording for it. Health Canada's antioxidant use is kept as a note.

review_flag.text: FDA, as of 1 May 2026: NAC is excluded from the definition of dietary supplement under section 201(ff)(3) of the FD&C Act, and FDA's guidance of August 2022 says it will use enforcement discretion for products that would be lawful dietary supplements if NAC were not excluded.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

sources.name: FDA: Information on Select Dietary Supplement Ingredients and Other Substances (NAC: Category 4, excluded under 201(ff)(3))
FDA guidance for industry: Policy Regarding N-acetyl-L-cysteine (August 2022)

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
